# std.deque

Double-ended queue: `Deque<T>`.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Deque`.

## `struct Deque<T>`

A queue with both ends open: `var q = Deque<Int>()`.

Fields: `buf: List<T>`, `head: Int`, `n: Int`, `mask: Int`, `want: Int`.

- `fn new() -> Deque<T>` — O(1); nothing is allocated until the first push; Create an empty `Deque<T>`.
- `fn of(xs: List<T>) -> Deque<T>` — O(n); A deque holding `xs`, front to back: the queue of a search, `var q = Deque.of(sources)`, then `while let u = q.pop_front(): ...`.
- `fn reserve(mut self, cap: Int)` — O(1) when empty, O(cap) otherwise; Reserve capacity for at least `cap` elements without reallocating.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — O(1); Number of elements currently in the deque.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — O(1); Whether the deque is empty.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — O(1); Remove all elements from the deque.
- `fn take(mut self) -> Deque<T>` — O(1); Move the deque's contents out in O(1), leaving `self` empty.
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — O(1) amortized; a full ring doubles; Append `x` to the back of the deque.
- `fn push_front(mut self, x: T)` — O(1) amortized; a full ring doubles; Prepend `x` to the front of the deque.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?T` — O(1); Remove and return the back, or `None` when empty.
- `fn pop_front(mut self) -> ?T` — O(1); Remove and return the front, or `None` when empty.
- `fn pop_front_while(mut self, ok: T -> Bool) -> List<T>` — O(k) for `k` removed
- `fn pop_while(mut self, ok: T -> Bool) -> List<T>` — O(k) for `k` removed; Pop from the back while `ok` holds; the popped values, back first.
- `@get fn first(self) -> ?T` — O(1); The front, or `None` when empty.
- `@get fn last(self, k: Int = 0) -> ?T` — O(1); The back, or `None` when empty.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `@get fn items(self) -> yields (Int, T)` — O(1) to make, O(1) per step; Each element with its place from the front: `for (i, x) in dq.items`.
- `fn get(self, i: Int) -> T` — O(1); The `i`-th element from the front.; traps: when `i` is not in `0..len`
- `fn set(mut self, i: Int, x: T)` — O(1); Overwrite the `i`-th element from the front (W8 `IndexSet` backing `dq[i] = x`).; traps: when `i` is not in `0..len`
- `fn to_list(self) -> List<T>` — O(n), one new `List`; Materialize the elements front to back as a `List<T>`.
- `fn each(self) -> yields T` — O(1) per step; Yield elements front to back without allocating.
- `fn each_rev(self) -> yields T` — O(1) per step; Yield elements back to front without allocating.
- `fn rotate_left(mut self, k: Int)` — O(min(k, n - k)) after reducing `k` mod `n`; Rotate elements left by `k` positions (`k` mod `len`).
- `fn rotate_right(mut self, k: Int)` — O(min(k, n - k)) after reducing `k` mod `n`; Rotate elements right by `k` positions (`k` mod `len`).

## `struct LinkedList<T>`

Doubly-linked list supporting O(1) end pushes/pops and O(1) splicing (`splice_back`, `splice_front`).

Fields: `head: Int`, `tail: Int`, `nx: List<Int>`, `pv: List<Int>`, `val: List<T>`, `flip: Bool`.

- `fn new() -> LinkedList<T>` — O(1); Create an empty `LinkedList<T>`.
- `fn of(x: T) -> LinkedList<T>` — O(1); Create a singleton `LinkedList<T>` containing `x`.
- `fn from_list(xs: List<T>) -> LinkedList<T>` — O(n); Build a `LinkedList<T>` from `xs`, front to back.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — O(1); Number of elements currently in the list.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — O(1); Whether the list is empty.
- `@get fn first(self) -> ?T` — O(1); The front element, or `None` when the list is empty (as `Deque.first`).
- `@get fn last(self) -> ?T` — O(1); The back element, or `None` when the list is empty (as `Deque.last`).
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — O(1); Append `x` to the back.
- `fn push_front(mut self, x: T)` — O(1); Prepend `x` to the front.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?T` — O(1); Remove and return the back element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn pop_front(mut self) -> ?T` — O(1); Remove and return the front element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn splice_back(mut self, other: LinkedList<T>)` — O(1); Splice all elements of `other` onto the back of `self`, consuming `other`.
- `fn splice_front(mut self, other: LinkedList<T>)` — O(1); Splice all elements of `other` onto the front of `self`, consuming `other`.
- `fn reverse(mut self)` — O(1); Reverse the list in place.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — O(1); Remove all elements.
- `fn each(self) -> yields T` — O(1) per step; Yield elements front to back.
- `fn each_rev(self) -> yields T` — O(1) per step; Yield elements back to front.

## Example

```cp
var dq = Deque<Int>()
dq.push(2)
dq.push_front(1)
dq.push(3)
print(dq.pop_front()!, dq.pop()!, dq.len)
// output: 1 3 1
```
